title: 3-Digit Addition and Subtraction Worksheets Within 1,000
intro: Use place-value models to teach addition and subtraction within 1,000.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Break an addend into hundreds, tens, and ones. For subtraction across a zero, show each exchange and record the renamed number.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

368 + 200 = 568
568 + 50 = 618
618 + 7 = 625

All three steps together add 257, so 368 + 257 = 625.

602 = 500 + 90 + 12
602 − 278 = 324
324 + 278 = 602

Ask your student

How can we rename this number without changing its value?

If your student needs help

If a regrouped digit is overlooked, rebuild the starting number and match each change to the written work.

Choosing and using the worksheet

These twelve horizontal questions allow room for working. The set can include zero and one-, two-, or three-digit numbers, and a quantity can reach 1,000. “Within 1,000” is an upper limit; this is not a set in which every number has exactly three digits. Use addition to check subtraction and compare the result with a rough estimate.
